extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and disciplinary authorities
extracted.subtask_description: An official USPTO Final Order imposing reciprocal discipline on a registered patent practitioner under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, describing procedural steps, the factual predicate, governing rules of professional conduct, and the specific sanctions and administrative requirements imposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, the USPTO Director may impose reciprocal discipline upon a practitioner identical to discipline imposed by a state court or other duly constituted authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states the Director filed a 'Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' requesting identical discipline to that imposed by the Nebraska Supreme Court. The Order applies the reciprocal discipline mechanism when the state-imposed discipline is established and no genuine issue of material fact exists under § 11.24(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and response procedure (40-day response period)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order provided Respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the Nebraska Supreme Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice was sent by certified mail and the practitioner is expected to file any opposition within 40 days of receipt; failure to file a response may result in a determination that there is no genuine issue of material fact and lead to imposition of identical discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: No genuine issue of material fact standard under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the practitioner fails to raise a genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), reciprocal discipline identical to the state-imposed sanction is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order concludes that because Respondent did not file a response, 'there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)' and the three-year suspension is appropriate. Respondents may oppose imposition by asserting one or more of the reasons provided in § 11.24(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation predicate: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's reciprocal discipline is predicated on his violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), having been disciplined by a duly constituted authority of a state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11.804(h) is cited as the rule breached (as applied here), indicating that being disciplined by a state authority serves as the predicate for USPTO reciprocal discipline proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nebraska rule of professional conduct § 3-508.4 misconduct categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Neb. Ct. R. of Prof. Cond. § 3-508.4 states: '[i]t is professional misconduct for a lawyer to: (a) violate or attempt to violate the Rules of Professional Conduct knowingly assist or induce another to do so through the acts of another; (b) commit a criminal act that reflects adversely on the lawyer's honesty, trustworthiness or fitness as a lawyer in other respects; (c) engage in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit or misrepresentation ...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Nebraska Supreme Court found the respondent admitted allegations that fell within these categories; such findings form the factual/legal basis for reciprocal discipline by the USPTO when adopted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underlying criminal conduct as disciplinary basis (false tax return)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent pled guilty to the charge of filing a false tax return for the tax year 2006, failing to report any gross receipts from his business activity and omitting gross receipts of $1,110,982.77.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explains that the underlying criminal conduct and its moral/ethical implications led to disciplinary proceedings and suspension by the Nebraska Supreme Court, and that such criminal acts reflect adversely on honesty/trustworthiness for purposes of professional discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order — Suspension from practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended for three years from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the USPTO, commencing on the date of this Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the principal disciplinary sanction imposed under the reciprocal discipline proceeding; it mirrors the three-year suspension imposed by the Nebraska Supreme Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order — Publication of Notice in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the following Notice in the Official Gazette: a Notice of Suspension describing the respondent, registration number, that reciprocal discipline was ordered for violating 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), and summarizing the underlying conduct and state court findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample Notice text included in the Order provides the content to be published (practitioner identity and registration number; statement of reciprocal discipline; summary of the underlying conviction and state disciplinary findings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Order — Notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted to practice, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement ensures other jurisdictions and relevant courts are notified of USPTO public discipline and its factual grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order — Compliance with duties in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Order does not restate § 11.58, it requires the disciplined practitioner to follow those duties (commonly involving client notification, file transfer, and related obligations upon suspension).

rubrics_metrics.name: Order — Dissociation from Customer Numbers and PKI certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate Respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure ("PKI") certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative disassociation severs the respondent's electronic access/credentials tied to USPTO filings while suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order — Prohibition on Customer Number access until reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, shall not obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor shall he have his name added to a USPTO Customer Number, unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prohibits any attempt to regain electronic filing or docketing privileges until formal reinstatement occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for action
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites the statutory and regulatory bases authorizing the USPTO to impose reciprocal discipline on registered practitioners.
